name: Question 12
problem:
Calculate 
${\sum }_{n=4}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{n}^{2}+4n+3}.$

*Hint: Try to factor the denominator first.*
worked_solution:
We can factor the denominator and use partial fractions to show that

$$
\frac{1}{{n}^{2}+4n+3}=\frac{1}{(n+1)(n+3)}=\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{n+1}-\frac{1}{n+3}).
$$

So, our series can be written as

$$
{\sum }_{n=4}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{n+1}-\frac{1}{n+3})=\frac{1}{2}{\sum }_{n=4}^{\infty }(\frac{1}{n+1}-\frac{1}{n+3}).
$$

Let's now compute the first few partial sums:

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{4} & =\frac{1}{2}[(\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7})] \\ {s}_{5} & =\frac{1}{2}[(\frac{1}{5}-\frac{1}{7})+(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{8})] \\ {s}_{6} & =\frac{1}{2}[(\frac{1}{5}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{8})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\frac{1}{9})] \\ {s}_{7} & =\frac{1}{2}[(\frac{1}{5}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\frac{1}{6}-\cancel{\frac{1}{8}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\frac{1}{9})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{8}}-\frac{1}{10})] \\ {s}_{8} & =\frac{1}{2}[(\frac{1}{5}-\cancel{\frac{1}{7}})+(\frac{1}{6}-\cancel{\frac{1}{8}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{7}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{9}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{8}}-\frac{1}{10})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{9}}-\frac{1}{11})]\end{aligned}
$$

We notice that all of the terms cancel except $\frac{1}{5},\frac{1}{6},$ and the $-\frac{1}{N+2}$ and  $-\frac{1}{N+3}$ terms. Therefore, the $N$th partial sum is

$$
{s}_{N}=\frac{1}{2}[\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{N+2}-\frac{1}{N+3}].
$$

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of ${s}_{N}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=4}^{\infty }\frac{1}{{n}^{2}+4n+3} & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }⁡{s}_{N} \\  & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }⁡\frac{1}{2}[\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{N+2}-\frac{1}{N+3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{N\to \infty }⁡[\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{6}-\frac{1}{N+2}-\frac{1}{N+3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{6}-0-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{6}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{11}{30} \\  & =\frac{11}{60}\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

We can factor the denominator and use partial fractions to show that

1n2+4n+3=1(n+1)(n+3)=12(1n+1−1n+3).

So, our series can be written as

∑n=4∞12(1n+1−1n+3)=12∑n=4∞(1n+1−1n+3).

Let's now compute the first few partial sums:

s4=12[(15−17)]s5=12[(15−17)+(16−18)]s6=12[(15−17)+(16−18)+(17−19)]s7=12[(15−17)+(16−18)+(17−19)+(18−110)]s8=12[(15−17)+(16−18)+(17−19)+(18−110)+(19−111)]

We notice that all of the terms cancel except 15,16, and the −1N+2 and −1N+3 terms. Therefore, the Nth partial sum is

sN=12[15+16−1N+2−1N+3].

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of sN:

∑n=4∞1n2+4n+3=limN→∞⁡sN=limN→∞⁡12[15+16−1N+2−1N+3]=12limN→∞⁡[15+16−1N+2−1N+3]=12[15+16−0−0]=12[15+16]=12⋅1130=1160
